name: Leave.EU

summary.text: Leave.EU Group Limited was a registered campaigner in the 2016 EU referendum, associated with Arron Banks. In May 2018 the Electoral Commission fined it £70,000 for breaches of electoral law including an incomplete spending return that omitted at least £77,380 in fees to Better for the Country Limited and incorrect reporting of three £6 million transactions from Banks. In February 2019 the ICO fined Leave.EU and Eldon Insurance a combined £120,000 for electronic marketing breaches. Cambridge Analytica and Leave.EU have both said that although Cambridge Analytica pitched for work, no contract was signed and no money changed hands.

facts.claim: The Electoral Commission fined Leave.EU a total of £70,000 for offences under PPERA, finding that it omitted at least £77,380 in fees paid to Better for the Country Limited, its campaign organiser, from its referendum spending return, and did not correctly report three regulated transactions from Arron Banks totalling £6 million.
facts.quote: Leave.EU also did not correctly report three regulated transactions from Mr Arron Banks, totalling £6 million.

facts.claim: The Commission said the unreported spending took Leave.EU over the £700,000 third-party spending cap by at least 10% and that the overspend may have been considerably higher; it referred a senior member of the campaign to the Metropolitan Police. Leave.EU said it would challenge the findings in court.
facts.quote: may well have been considerably higher than that

facts.claim: The Electoral Commission's investigation did not find evidence that Leave.EU paid for services from Cambridge Analytica during the referendum campaign period; Cambridge Analytica and Leave.EU have said that the consultancy pitched for work but had no contract and no money changed hands.
facts.quote: while the consultancy pitched for work with Leave.EU, it did not have any contracts and no money changed hands

facts.claim: The ICO's November 2018 report recorded a notice of intent to fine Leave.EU for a breach of PECR after almost 300,000 emails to Eldon Insurance (GoSkippy) customers contained a Leave.EU newsletter, and said it was investigating allegations that Eldon shared customer data with Leave.EU; it found no evidence that the 'Big Data Dolphins' project ever functioned or that UK citizens' data was transferred to the University of Mississippi.
facts.quote: We found no evidence that Big Data Dolphins ever actually functioned

facts.claim: In February 2019 the ICO fined Leave.EU and Eldon Insurance a combined £120,000 for electronic marketing breaches, finding that systems for segregating insurance customers' data from political subscribers' data were ineffective, and said it would audit both companies.
facts.quote: systems for segregating the personal data of insurance customers' from that of political subscribers' were ineffective
